title: After-PR Checks Build Plan
eyebrow: Build plan for approval · "After every pull request, a check makes sure it says how to test it and what's next" · nothing built yet

short.lead: Four steps, built by me one at a time on the branch AjsAgent/after-pr-answers, then one pull request that answers its own two questions. One finding affects the agent name step (step 4). In this cloud session git's name is "Claude" and the account name is "aydenjwilkins", and cloud sessions never run your setup scripts. Without a fix, commits made in cloud sessions would be credited to "aydenjwilkins's agent". The choice below decides what name cloud sessions use.
short.hint: Tap a step for what it changes and how it is checked.
items: file
PR body
Step 1: a pull request must answer both questions

The GitHub tool and gh pr create refuse a pull request body with no "How to test it in a new session" heading or no "What's next" heading. The refusal names the missing heading and the fix. The issue is "A pull request body must say how to test it and what's next".
Checked by three self-test cases: both headings missing, one missing, and both present.
check
QA page
Step 2: a QA page must carry both

make_page.py's QA mode needs a qa.test list (each step: the exact prompt and what proves it) and a qa.next list (each item: what it waits on). It refuses the build without them, naming the field. The issue is "A QA page must carry its test steps and what's next".
Checked by self-test cases for each missing list and for a page with both.
stop
Reply
Step 3: the reply reporting a pull request answers both

A new check that runs at the end of each reply. If I opened a pull request while answering your message, or the reply says one was merged, the reply must either link a page or give both answers (how to test it, and what's next). If it does neither, the reply is blocked once, with the fix named. The issue is "A reply reporting a pull request answers how to test it and what's next".
Checked by four self-test cases, including that a turn with no pull request is untouched.
swap
Your name
Step 4: the agent name is configurable

One function gives the name to every credit line, branch prefix and identity notice. HOUSE_RULES_AGENT_NAME wins, then the git name (ignoring a trailing "'s agent", and ignoring the name "Claude" that cloud sessions set), then the account name before the @. tools/install.py, which the setup scripts run, writes HOUSE_RULES_AGENT_NAME=AJ on your machines. The issue is "Agent name, credit and branch prefix are configurable, not hard-coded to AJ".
Checked by self-test cases for each source and for the order between them.
hand

You test the pull request
you
One pull request, version 2.69.0, whose own body is the first one checked by step 1.
The pull request's "How to test it in a new session" section gives you the exact prompts.

changes: Refuses a body missing either answer, naming it.
Applies to both ways I open a pull request: the GitHub tool and gh pr create.
Every QA page then shows the test steps and what's next.
Blocks once, like the other end-of-reply checks.
The two heading names are defined once in hook.py, so all three checks use the same ones.
From hard-coded "AJ" to one configurable name.
Each user's own name, with yours kept as AJ
The 19 lines in hook.py that hard-code "AJ's agent" or AjsAgent/ will call the new name function instead.
choices: In a cloud session, where git's name is "Claude" and no setup script runs, where should the name AJ come from?
Repositories owned by Ajw2003 default to AJ
The plugin already knows your GitHub owner name. A session in one of your repositories gets AJ with nothing to set; anyone else's repositories use their own name.
You set HOUSE_RULES_AGENT_NAME=AJ in your cloud environment
Fully generic, but a one-time setting in each cloud environment's variables, and until then the credit reads "aydenjwilkins's agent".
Without one of these, every cloud session would credit a name you did not choose.
